messages.subject: permutation test with mr-imp
parts:
I have a densely mapped (~1cM) cross with a fair amount of missing info
(~20% of the markers missing data on half the individuals in the
cross). I'm using multiple imputation with the function
sim.geno(cross, n.draws=16) to impute the missing info, then using
"mr-imp" method for mapping. When I try to use the "n.perm" function I
receive the following error: "Error in clean(cross): object
"tempcross" not found". I've also tried a single imputation and
received the same error. I have two questions:

1.) Is this the most appropriate way to deal with the missing data?

2.) Why can't I run permutations to determine an empirical threshold,
and if I continue to use multiple imputation how do I calculate
significance thresholds?

Thanks!!!
-Charles

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: permutation test with mr-imp
parts:
If you use scanone with method="mr-imp", all missing data
are replaced with a single imputation.

It's better to do sim.geno (probably with n.draws=128 or so)
and then when you run scanone(), use method="imp".

The problem you were having with method="mr-imp" with the imputations
was a bug. It'll be fixed in the next version.

karl
